summary: Markets are treading cautiously ahead of the Federal Reserve's October decision, expected at 2pm ET today, with Chair Kevin Warsh widely anticipated to hold rates steady after September's surprise hike. The decision comes as persistent inflation linked to elevated oil prices—with Brent near $111—and upcoming midterm elections complicate the outlook. Equities rallied Tuesday on strong AI momentum: the S&P 500 gained 0.6% to 7,722.60 and the Nasdaq surged 1.2% to 26,477.81, driven by SK Hynix's record earnings and Anthropic's IPO filing. Bitcoin reclaimed $81,000 with $176 million in ETF inflows, while Ethereum held near $2,340 despite continued outflows. Earnings season delivered sharp divergences: Vertiv and Phillips 66 crushed expectations, while Enphase and Boston Scientific disappointed. Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close, setting the stage for a critical test of the AI infrastructure trade.

signals.title: Fed holds rates steady after September hike, eyes December move
signals.desc: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep rates unchanged today after raising in September for the first time since 2023, but markets will parse Chair Warsh's comments for signals on December policy amid stubborn inflation driven by Iran-linked oil surges.

signals.title: SK Hynix blowout earnings ignite global chip rally
signals.desc: SK Hynix reported a 632% surge in operating profit and sold-out memory capacity through 2029, sending its shares up over 10% and lifting Samsung, the Kospi 6.6%, and U.S. semiconductor stocks, reinforcing the AI infrastructure demand thesis.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $176M inflow, second consecutive day
signals.desc: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows of $176 million on October 27, marking a second straight day of institutional demand as BTC reclaimed $81,000 ahead of the Fed decision and Big Tech earnings.

signals.title: Oil surges above $111 on Iran escalation fears
signals.desc: Brent crude jumped 1.5% to $111 and WTI rose 1.6% to $101.50 amid reports that Washington has asked Gulf states to prepare for a possible post-midterm campaign against Iran, keeping inflation and rate-hike expectations elevated.

signals.title: Data center stocks split: Vertiv soars, Enphase crashes on rate sensitivity
signals.desc: Vertiv surged 13.3% after doubling orders and raising guidance, while Enphase plunged 15.8% citing higher rates and an expired tax credit hurting home solar demand, highlighting sector divergence ahead of the Fed decision.

verdict: Fed decision day dominates with rates expected on hold but hawkish guidance likely given oil-driven inflation, while mega-cap tech earnings tonight will determine whether the AI rally has legs or fades into year-end risk-off.
